author: cinammoncroc000
body:
As of recently, there has been a lot of discussion around maps and this gameplay vs. aesthetics philosophy. Seeing that there have been a lot of complaints around newer maps "not having good gameplay," I've decided to make a thread where we could discuss on how to make maps with good gameplay, since I've realized that, well, I don't know "how" to do that. As a beginner map creator, I'd like to hear others' inputs on this, and anyone can use this as a reference when creating a map.

Keep in mind that even though this discussion was mainly focusing on Nebula (and Nexus, I guess,) I want to keep it open to all of Avicus' minigames (CTH, Walls, Avicade, etc.)

Without further ado, I'll start off a discussion.
What makes good gameplay in a Nebula map? More specifically, how do older, popular maps (like Quintus and Rendezvous) play better than some newer maps? (like Honeycomb)

replies.author: _Phyre
replies.body: On nexus, there are a ton of maps where you can strafe, thats all i need, i h8 block-hitting when your in tight spaces. So i would recommend doing Gameplay first then thinking of aesthetics.. and on Nebula good gameplay is when you have 25% Aesthetics 75% Gameplay (in my opinion) then moving on to the monuments, should be East but at the same time hard to get :P

replies.author: smitdalt
replies.body: Well, for me the things that affect gameplay on a map are the void gap between islands (if there are islands,) how hard/easy it is to get the monument(s), and where on the map the main fight is going on.

replies.author: jracer15
replies.body: The best way to have a feel for the gameplay is to feel like your playing the map and think where would I go to?  How would I make it to the monument?  Now Nebula hard for new gameplay because there is soo many strategies but I'm sure if you have an idea of new gameplay think of ways the map can make that happen!

replies.author: Ogrey
replies.body:
What I mainly do is grab a piece of paper and start making symmetrical lines, then getting more and more ideas, keep drawing, thinking and you can even use other sources of inspiration (like other games, for instance, and on my case: Oeilvert from Final Fantasy IX, Cleyra from Final Fantasy IX, Formorgar Mines from Tibia, Continent of Zao from Tibia, Windmill Plains from Diddy Kong Racing, other sources of inspiration, like Justice series, inspired by Total Drama: All Stars, or even real-life locations, such as Yellowstone National Park.

While building, always keep places symmetrical, and keep your working area organized. Always think of new ways to add gameplay features (buildings may be seen for some as aesthetic-wise map parts, but if you think about it, buildings and structures do play an important part, if well built, well designed, well located and well used). Never stay with the first sketch of your map, always make place for new ideas, unique concepts and fun gameplay styles (Here are some early concept sketches for Windmill Plains and Justice 3)
You can also add some unique features to the map via YML (Maybe fireball bows, sign loadouts, multiple player spawns, healing zones, telepads, jump pads, whatever you wish!). Enchantment Tables and Beacons also provide variety (as seen in Yellowstone) allowing even more "paths to take". Correct placement of monuments, correct spawn location, correct front line designs, correct amount of resources (such as iron or chests containing special items), all those may induce different gameplay styles on a map, either in a good or bad way, depends on how you build it.
